newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota Twins stadium plan under attack - paper.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota Twins stadium plan under attack - paper.

text.p: Plans for a new $350 million stadium for the Minnesota Twins American League baseball team have come under attack by some state lawmakers, Minneapolis Star Tribune reported Thursday.
The newspaper said some legislators were calling for Henry Savelkoul, chairman of the Metropolitan Sports facilities Commission and Gov. Arne Carlson's chief negotiator on the stadium, to step down.
Other lawmakers expressed dissatisfaction with the funding plan proposed by Carlson earlier this month, the paper said.

That plan called for a 10-cent hike in the state cigarette tax to fund the state's portion of the project. The team's owner has pledged more than $157.5 million in construction and operating costs and offered the state a 49 percent ownership stake in the team.
The news out of the state capital follows the release of a poll Sunday by the newspaper that showed 69 percent of respondants opposed to the plan.
